examples.text: That wasn't an accident! You did it on purpose!

raw_glosses: (idiomatic) By design, as opposed to by accident; intentionally; deliberately.
glosses: By design, as opposed to by accident; intentionally; deliberately.

examples.text: Blifil bowed and stammered, and looked like a fool; but Western, without giving him time to form a speech for the purpose, answered, “Well, well, I am to blame, if you will, I always am, certainly; but come, let the girl be fetched back again, or let Mr Blifil go to her.——He’s come up on purpose, and there is no time to be lost.”
examples.ref: 1749, Henry Fielding, The History of Tom Jones, a Foundling:

examples.text: I send this to the town, on purpose to have it reach you by the earliest post […].
examples.ref: 1792, Charlotte Smith, Desmond, Broadview, published 2001, page 260:

raw_glosses: (now rare) In order to (do something); with the objective that.
glosses: In order to (do something); with the objective that.
